clue.text: Judges and paparazzi in lift

parts.note: judges collectively are the bench
photographers and reporters collectively are the press

explanation.surface: A judge and some photographers find themselves crammed into an elevator together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator, but here it is a weightlifting exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym exercise in which a barbell is pushed up from the chest while lying flat is a type of lift.

clue.text: Booze improved when less sober

indicators.note: less tells us to take letters away from the word before it

parts.note: something improved is better
TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays sober

explanation.surface: A drinker claims alcohol makes things better once one stops being sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes both Ts of TT (teetotal) from BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale and lager are alcoholic drinks, a common kind of booze.

clue.text: Gossip column's latest exploit reported

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one, here the last of column
reported says we hear a word spoken rather than see it written

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A tabloid gossip column's most recent scoop gets talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb USE is said 'yooz', which sounds like the end of the answer after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is talk about recent happenings, a loose synonym for current information.

clue.text: Dramatist rather shakily holding worn-out leg

indicators.note: holding means the anagram wraps round the other pieces
shakily suggests the letters of rather are jumbled about

parts.note: something worn-out is old
pin is informal for a leg

explanation.surface: A playwright wobbles about, supporting a tired leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakily' rearranges RATHER as HAR...TER, which is 'holding' OLD and PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel-winning British playwright wrote The Birthday Party and The Caretaker.

clue.text: Souvenir left by one in sports ground

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the sports ground

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a public sports field
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone has left a keepsake behind at a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: A REC is a British recreation ground, a public park for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name an object kept as a reminder of the past.

clue.text: One taking charge has better personality during day

indicators.note: during means the next pieces sit inside the day

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
to cap something is to better or outdo it
ego is one's sense of self or personality

explanation.surface: A new leader with a stronger character takes charge during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking charge' looks like assuming command; it means accepting blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A person made to bear blame, or charges, for others' faults is this kind of victim.

clue.text: Regularly distributed gang head over the hill

indicators.note: regularly distributed picks every other letter, the second, fourth and so on, of gang head

explanation.surface: A gang leader past their prime gets handed out regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone over the hill is past their best through being old.

clue.text: Mostly pleased with agents breaking into geological development

indicators.note: mostly tells us to drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: pleased means glad
the CIA is the US agency of secret agents

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of into are broken up and reset

explanation.surface: Happy spies storm into some geological process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' looks like a container but 'breaking' rearranges INTO to make the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The forming and spreading of ice sheets over land is a geological process.

clue.text: Weaken one ignited during argument

indicators.note: during means the next pieces sit inside the argument

parts.note: a debate is a formal argument
I is the Roman numeral for one
something ignited has been lit

explanation.surface: Someone who sets a fire mid-quarrel only undermines their case.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap someone's strength is to enfeeble or weaken them.

clue.text: He wrote senselessly to harass leader governing electoral area

indicators.note: governing here means holding sway over, so the anagram surrounds the ward
to harass is to harry or disturb, so the letters of leader are knocked about

parts.note: a ward is an electoral district

explanation.surface: A writer pesters a party leader in charge of a constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to harass' rearranges LEADER as ED...LEAR, 'governing' (holding) WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author is famous for nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat.

clue.text: Sweet, innocent thing reportedly hit

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: A gentle, harmless soul is said to have been struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep is the classic image of meek innocence.

clue.text: Shock pastor inwardly, with odd hints about primates

indicators.note: inwardly keeps only the inside letters of pastor
about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
odd says the letters of hints are set out in a strange order

parts.note: men are human beings, who are primates

explanation.surface: A minister is shocked by strange suggestions about apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' gives ASTO; 'odd' rearranges HINTS as NISH...T, 'about' MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Great surprise or amazement is a feeling of shock.

clue.text: Music player, sleeping rough, covered hair

indicators.note: covered means the anagram wraps round the next piece
rough suggests the letters of sleeping are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A homeless musician sleeps on the street with hair hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SLEEPING as G...ENSPIEL, which has 'covered' LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion instrument of tuned metal bars is a thing that plays music.

clue.text: John signed this article, rejected by journal, on speech of ex- president

parts.note: mag, short for magazine, is a journal

indicators.note: rejected means the article is sent back, read the other way

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: on speech of says we take how the next word sounds when spoken

parts.note: Jimmy Carter is a former US president

explanation.surface: A former president's speech is reported, with an article turned down by a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: CARTER said in a British accent, with no final R, sounds like the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: King John of England put his seal to the 1215 charter of liberties at Runnymede.

clue.text: Old engineer puts his foot down to keep female working

indicators.note: to keep means the steps hold the next piece inside

parts.note: someone who puts a foot down steps
a hen is a female bird
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A veteran engineer insists firmly that a woman stays employed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts his foot down' looks like insisting; it is just stepping.
explanation.definitionFit: George, the 19th-century railway pioneer, built the Rocket locomotive.

clue.text: Food worker over in heart of Ethiopia

parts.note: a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

indicators.note: in places the next piece inside the heart
heart of takes the central letters of Ethiopia

parts.note: something over is past

explanation.surface: A labourer has finished in the middle of an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats and pickles is food served first.

clue.text: Star's late meal half-heartedly eaten in the end (eggs)

indicators.note: half-heartedly drops one of the two central letters

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: in the end takes the last letter of eaten

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A celebrity's late dinner of eggs is eaten without enthusiasm at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one P from SUPPER's middle pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding star that suddenly blazes far brighter is a type of star.

clue.text: Rowing crew starts to examine training after a month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of examine and training

explanation.surface: A rowing eight begins assessing training a month on.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat's eight oarsmen form a group of eight, the musical term for such a group.

clue.text: Quickly enter current number when withdrawing (personal ID)

indicators.note: withdrawing means going back, so current and number are read backwards

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: At a cash machine, quickly type the current code when taking money out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop somewhere briefly is to make a quick visit, idiomatically.

clue.text: Preferred to rearrange attic when storing old garment

parts.note: a pet project is a preferred one

indicators.note: when storing means the anagram holds the next piece
to rearrange says the letters of attic are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone tidies the loft, where an old item of clothing is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rearrange' makes TTICAT from ATTIC, 'storing' O.
explanation.definitionFit: An underskirt worn beneath a dress is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Centre for kids includes farm that is shortly to manufacture dairy produce

indicators.note: includes means the nursery wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a creche is a day nursery for small children

indicators.note: to manufacture says the letters are made into something new

parts.note: i.e. is the short form of that is

explanation.surface: A children's centre with a farm makes its own dairy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manufacture' turns FARM and IE into MEFRAI, which CRECHE 'includes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick soured cream from France is a product of the dairy.

clue.text: United captain on edge somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A football club's skipper is a little nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together into a single whole are united, in the phrase all in a single unit.

clue.text: Noise from one scoffing? That man's getting seconds

parts.note: his means belonging to that man

explanation.surface: A greedy eater's noise as he helps himself to second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' looks like gobbling food; it means jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibilant sound of contempt is what a jeering audience makes.

clue.text: Gamble on a trial version

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager on a software test release.
explanation.definitionFit: Software released for testing before launch is in its second Greek-letter stage.

clue.text: Pause on empty seat

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: empty removes the inside, leaving only the outer letters of seat

explanation.surface: Take a break on a vacant chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A break from activity, or a musical silence, is a stop or pause.

clue.text: Make the same unsettling noise carrying grand into house

indicators.note: into means the assembled letters go inside the house

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: carrying means the anagram holds the next piece
unsettling suggests the letters of noise are disturbed

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A disturbing sound makes everything uniform as a piano is hauled indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' rearranges NOISE; 'carrying' G gives OGENIS, put 'into' HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To process something until it is uniform throughout is to make it consistent.

clue.text: Six-footer embraces posh relative

indicators.note: embraces means the insect wraps round the next piece

parts.note: an ant is an insect with six feet
U is short for upper class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A very tall person hugs an upper-class family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is a six-legged insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family relation.

clue.text: What skinny-dipper is at Ness swimming in mass of cold water?

parts.note: someone swimming naked is bare

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of at Ness are moving about

explanation.surface: A naked swimmer at Loch Ness wonders about a body of chilly water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Ocean's arm north of Norway and Russia is a large expanse of icy sea.
